_doc: Tier-B treks (generated by tools/trails/osm_tail.py from OpenStreetMap, ODbL, and the Copernicus DEM; never edit by hand).

trails.name: Koshu douchu
trails.why: The Kōshū Kaidō was one of the five routes of the Edo period. It was built to connect Edo with Kai Province in modern-day Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan.

trails.name: Old road near Jōetsu (北国街道（信越）)
trails.why: The Hokkoku Kaidō was a highway in Japan during the Edo period. It was a secondary route, ranked below the Edo Five Routes in importance.

trails.name: Kumano Kodo - Kohechi
trails.why: The Kohechi is one of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage routes, linking Koyasan with Kumano Hongu Taisha across the Kii Mountains.

trails.name: Tokai Nature Trail near Nagoya
trails.why: The Tōkai Nature Trail is a long distance walkway that traverses 11 prefectures and covers 1,697 kilometres, running from Meiji no Mori Takao Quasi-National Park in Tokyo to Meiji no Mori Minō Quasi-National Park in Osaka Prefecture.

trails.name: Old road near Osaka (京街道)
trails.why: The Kyo Kaido, also called the Osaka Kaido, was the road linking Osaka and Kyoto.

trails.name: Old road near Kasukabe (日光道中)
trails.why: The Nikkō Kaidō was one of the five routes of the Edo period and it was built to connect Edo with the temple-shrine complex of the Mangan-ji and Tōshōsha, which are located in the present-day city of Nikkō, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan.

trails.name: Suihei-Trail
trails.why: The Suihei-hodo path near "Odaiko", a section cut into the cliff; the hanging wire is a remnant of the logs once suspended from the rock as a walkway.

trails.name: Old road near Nagahama (北国街道 (近江))
trails.why: The Hokkoku Kaido was a road built under the Edo shogunate linking the Kinki region with Hokuriku over the Tochinoki Pass.

trails.name: Daibosatsu Loop
trails.why: Mount Daibosatsu stands in the Yamanashi side of Chichibu-Tama-Kai National Park. The peak itself is in Kōshū, Yamanashi.

trails.name: Konpira-yama
trails.why: Easily accessible, feel the power of volcanoes Open: Late April through mid-November This course takes you around the remains of the Mt. Usu from the eruption in 2000.
